factual_methodology.summary: Primary institutional releases distinguish September actuals, October forecasts and August trade values; no unverified 17 October spot prices; numbers presented with period and limits.

editorial_publication_readiness.summary: Refined diesel supply and crude export recovery constitute a distinct question from the preceding border-price analysis; no unapproved editorial meta-language or false causal inference.

visual_evidence_readiness.summary: Two aligned charts using sourced 4.7/1.9 and 1.5/1.7 values; three evidence tables, two-chain causal flow and five-region qualitative map in each locale.

research_depth.summary: Physical supply, refinery output, stock location, European trade, income effects and three falsifiable scenarios in both languages.

evidence_traceability.summary: Eleven institutional URLs per locale, seven primary-source hosts; explicit dates and qualification of estimates, projections and nominal trade figures.

counterfactual_review.summary: Tests downstream recovery, diesel-constrained crude recovery and demand-destruction scenarios; challenges one-to-one pass-through and attribution of aggregate deficits to energy.

contrary_evidence: Higher crude exports and lower oil demand may ease some fuels even if diesel remains constrained.
The euro-area external deficit reflects nominal values of multiple traded product categories, not only energy.
August trade and September inflation reports cover separate periods and do not establish causal diesel pass-through.
limitations: Some current institutional figures are preliminary estimates or projections subject to revision.
No calibrated estimate of diesel-specific inflation contribution or causal impact on GDP, yields or income.
Editorial QA performed in this publication workflow, not independent external peer review.
notes: Internal documentary QA against repository content and sourced methodology, with bilingual parity and hash-bound source integrity.
